title: Contours Tell You Parts, Not Cavities: an Identifiability Boundary for Orthographic Three-View Reconstruction, with Semantic Part Assembly and Confidence-Weighted Solid Priors
description:
Background. Reconstructing 3D shape from three orthographic silhouettes is deceptively under-constrained. We make the boundary explicit and build two practical methods on the observable side of it.

Contributions. (1) Theorem 1 (identifiability boundary): for any object whose exterior is axis-visible, the visual-hull error set equals exactly the union of enclosed cavities — closed cavities carry zero information in contours, for per-part or joint methods alike. (2) Semantic part assembly: shared-frame per-part reconstruction gated by a leave-one-out semantic compatibility table recovers part-contact topology exactly (35 synthetic objects × 7 conditions; all three pre-registered criteria pass: Chamfer −21.3%, graph errors −100% vs no-semantics and no-shared-frame ablations). (3) Confidence-weighted solid priors: a hull-gated solid-volume regularizer with warmup fixes the false-cavity pathology of contour-only SDF fitting (−75.5%, p=0.039 primary; −72.9%, p=8e-5 pooled; disclosures in the paper) and reveals an all-solid attractor explosion as a dose-dependent failure mode. (4) Real-geometry transfer: three ABO product models, split and voxelized fully automatically, yield exact contact recovery and 1–2% world-normalized Chamfer with zero-shot semantic transfer.

Artifacts. The deposit includes the full paper draft, all experimental code, per-run records, figures, and an independent verification suite (98 assertions, 0 mismatches). A public repository with a one-command reproduction (≈3 min, cached results) accompanies this deposit; see related identifiers.
